digest.component_or_area: development process and code quality metrics
propositions: No current bug record contains detected_by metadata, preventing calculation of true escaped-defect rate or detection-stage efficiency; caused_by links are advisory and demonstrably noisy due to blame-attribution selection effects.

Plan-review adoption rose from 29.2% (Q2) to 79.5% (Q3) for review-before-claim, with first-pass rate at 49.0% and median 2 attempts/p90 8 attempts; the 116,560 LLM calls per 114.72 per accepted completion-PASS represents mixed-cohort operational load rather than unit cost.

Completion first-pass is 72.3% (722/998); Testing-section tickets showed 79.7% versus 68.6% without headings, and file-impact declarations 74.2% versus 67.6% undeclared—observational correlations without causal evidence.

Q2-to-Q3 commit governance adoption reached near-complete: ticket trailer 0%→90.4%, DCO 0%→82.9%, Change-Id 0%→99.3%; source diffs decreased (median 111.5→95 lines) while test co-change increased (median 84.5→160.5 lines on source changes).

Thirty-five source modules at or above 720 LOC (four at 790-800 LOC: inbound_differ.py, binding_store.py, apply_inbound_records.py, signing.py, llm/runner.py) and 4.09% code duplication represent debt pressure; same-file retouch within 24h was 47.7% of consecutive file-touch pairs—a hotspot/coordination proxy, not proven rework.

Authorship concentration is 92.4% in top operator/bot accounts; code-review first-pass is 97.4%, but reviewer/vote independence and external-contributor path were not audited, so governance artifacts alone do not prove sustainable maintainership or prevent single-provider resilience risk.
